mainTopic: How much liquid cancels a forbidden mouse (the rule of sixty), and when wine left with a נכרי becomes forbidden.
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of a mouse that fell into a drink. It asks about vinegar, and רב אשי rejects a proof from רב כהנא's ruling because that mouse had fallen apart. רבינא suggests that 101 times the mouse's size cancels it, like תרומה, but רב תחליפא בר גיזא compares it to strong-tasting spices. רב אחאי gives 50 for vinegar and רב שמואל בריה דרב איקא gives 60 for beer. The הלכה is 60 for both, and for all Torah prohibitions. Then a new משנה teaches when wine left with a נכרי becomes forbidden as יין נסך. The test in its cases is whether the נכרי expects the ישראל back at any moment, and how long an announced absence must be. The גמרא explains 'presumed to be watched' with a ברייתא about workers carrying pure items. It asks why the two halves of that ברייתא differ, and רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if the mouse fell into vinegar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is when a mouse falls into vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a mouse fell into vinegar, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the earlier case of a mouse in beer to a new case: a mouse that fell into vinegar. It asks what the law is, and this sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a mixture becomes forbidden depends on whether the forbidden thing adds a good taste or a bad taste. Vinegar has a sharp taste of its own, so the גמרא is not sure how the mouse affects it.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'mouse' is not in this line. The גמרא assumes you remember that the topic is a mouse that fell into a drink.

phrases.english: If it fell into vinegar, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the mouse from the earlier discussion. The גמרא leaves the word out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the earlier mouse-in-beer discussion to a new liquid, vinegar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a mouse that fell into vinegar make the vinegar forbidden? In other words, does it add a good taste to the vinegar?

steps.title: A story from רב כהנא's house
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל tells רב אשי that this exact case happened at רב כהנא's house, and רב כהנא forbade the vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הלל said to רב אשי: There was such a case in the house of רב כהנא, and רב כהנא forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הלל tries to answer the question with a real-life ruling: רב כהנא forbade vinegar that a mouse fell into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הלל's reasoning is that if רב כהנא forbade the vinegar, the mouse must add a good taste to it. So the answer to the question would be 'forbidden.'

keyTerms.meaning: The house or study hall of the רב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִילֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi:
There was an incident in the house of Rav Kahana,
and Rav Kahana forbade it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a precedent to answer the question in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a mouse in vinegar makes the vinegar forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practical ruling of רב כהנא, who forbade such vinegar.

steps.title: That mouse had fallen apart
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof: in that story the mouse had broken into pieces, so that is the reason it was forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That mouse had fallen apart into pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says the story proves nothing about taste, because in that case the mouse had come apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the mouse breaks into pieces, someone could swallow an actual piece of it, and that is forbidden no matter what the taste is. So רב כהנא's ruling may have nothing to do with taste, and the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: It completely fell apart into pieces.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the vinegar is permitted. He only says this story cannot prove anything about taste.

phrases.english: He said to him: That one had completely fallen apart.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב אשי. Since the mouse came apart, small pieces could be eaten along with the vinegar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רב כהנא's ruling. It does not decide the original question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story had a special detail: the mouse fell apart. That gives a separate reason to forbid the vinegar, apart from taste.

steps.title: רבינא measures at 101, like תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא thought the mouse is cancelled in 101 times its size. He reasoned it should be no stricter than תרומה, which a משנה says is cancelled at 101.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא thought to measure it at one hundred and one. He said: It is no worse than תרומה, as we learned in a משנה: תרומה is cancelled in one hundred and one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a new question: how much liquid is needed to cancel the mouse. רבינא suggests 101 times its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא compares the mouse to תרומה. תרומה mixed into regular food is cancelled when there are 100 parts of regular food for each part of תרומה, so 101 in total. He argues a mouse should need no more than that.

keyTerms.meaning: To measure or set an amount.
The portion of produce given to a כהן, forbidden to others.
Is cancelled (literally, 'goes up') in a mixture.

phrases.english: Ravina thought to measure it at one hundred and one,
phrases.notes: He means 101 times the mouse's size in liquid.

phrases.english: he said: It is no worse than terumah,
as we learned: Terumah is cancelled in one hundred and one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from whether the vinegar is forbidden to how much liquid cancels the mouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mouse is cancelled in 101 times its volume, because it should be no stricter than תרומה.

steps.title: Maybe it is like spices of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר גיזא pushes back: maybe the mouse is like spices of תרומה in a pot, whose taste is never cancelled even at 101.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא בר גיזא said to רבינא: Perhaps it is like spices of תרומה in a pot, whose taste is not cancelled!
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא בר גיזא questions רבינא's comparison to regular תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not all תרומה follows the 101 rule. Spices have a strong taste that stays noticeable even in a large mixture. The mouse might be like that, so 101 might not be enough.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר גִּיזָּא לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa bar Giza said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא כְּתַבְלִין שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה בִּקְדֵירָה דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: Perhaps it is like spices of terumah in a pot,
whose taste is not cancelled!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא כְּתַבְלִין שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה בִּקְדֵירָה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison רבינא made in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבינא's comparison of the mouse to ordinary תרומה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The mouse's taste may be strong like spices, and the taste of spices of תרומה is not cancelled at 101.

steps.title: 50 for vinegar, 60 for beer
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי measured the mouse in vinegar at 50. רב שמואל בריה דרב איקא measured it in beer at 60.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי measured vinegar at fifty. רב שמואל בריה דרב איקא measured beer at sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give actual amounts: 50 times for vinegar and 60 times for beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar is sharp, so it covers the mouse's taste with less liquid. Beer is milder, so it needs the usual amount of 60.

keyTerms.meaning: He measured or set the amount.

phrases.english: Rav Achai measured vinegar at fifty,
Rav Shmuel, son of Rav Ika,
measured beer at sixty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא's 101 was challenged, gives different amounts for each liquid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mouse is cancelled in 50 times its size in vinegar (רב אחאי) and in 60 times its size in beer (רב שמואל בריה דרב איקא).

steps.title: The הלכה: sixty for everything
steps.stepSummary: The final הלכה is that both vinegar and beer need 60, and so does every Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: both this and that are at sixty, and so too all prohibitions in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: 60 for vinegar, 60 for beer, and 60 for all Torah prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה does not follow רב אחאי's lighter amount of 50 for vinegar. It also does not follow רבינא's 101. Sixty becomes one standard measure for cancelling forbidden taste.
steps.whatToRemember: A forbidden food mixed into permitted food is cancelled when there is 60 times as much permitted food. This applies to vinegar, beer, and all Torah prohibitions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is a major source for the well-known rule of ביטול בששים (cancellation in sixty) in practical כשרות.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: this and that are at sixty,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means both the vinegar and the beer.

phrases.english: and so too all prohibitions in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the amounts given in steps 4 and 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both vinegar and beer cancel the mouse at 60, and 60 is the measure for all Torah prohibitions.

steps.title: A נכרי carrying wine barrels together with a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a נכרי carries wine barrels with a ישראל and the wine counts as watched, it is permitted. If the ישראל said he was going far away, the wine is forbidden only if he was gone long enough for the barrel to be opened and resealed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a longer amount of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A נכרי was carrying barrels of wine from place to place together with a ישראל. If the wine was considered watched, it is permitted. If the ישראל told him he was going far away, the wine is forbidden if he was gone long enough for the נכרי to bore a hole, plug it, and let the plug dry. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: it is forbidden only if he was gone long enough to open the barrel, close it with a new stopper, and let the stopper dry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. Its first case is a נכרי and a ישראל carrying wine barrels together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear is that the נכרי secretly opened a barrel and made the wine into יין נסך. As long as the נכרי expects the ישראל back at any moment, he would not risk it, so the wine is permitted. If the ישראל said he was going far away, the question is whether there was enough time to open a barrel and hide the evidence. The תנא קמא says boring a small hole and plugging it is enough. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it must be enough time to remove the whole stopper and make a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: Considered watched, meaning the wine is treated as supervised
That he bore a small hole in the barrel's seal
And it dries, so the new plug looks untouched

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'enough time to bore, seal and dry' does not mean the wine is forbidden right away. It means the wine is forbidden only if the ישראל was gone at least that long.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A non-Jew who was transporting
barrels of wine together with a Jew
from place to place,
if it was considered watched, it is permitted.
If he told him that he was going far away,
it is forbidden if there was enough time for him to bore a hole, plug it, and let it dry.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּפְתַּח אֶת הֶחָבִית וְיִגּוֹף וְתִיגּוֹב.
phrases.english: Enough time for him to open the barrel, stop it up, and let it dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נׇכְרִי שֶׁהָיָה מַעֲבִיר עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּדֵּי יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier discussion of how much is needed to cancel a forbidden item ended at step 7. This is a brand-new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine that counts as watched stays permitted. If the ישראל announced a long absence, the wine is forbidden only if he was gone long enough to bore, seal and dry (תנא קמא), or to open, re-stop and dry (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).

steps.title: Wine left on a wagon or ship while the owner takes a shortcut
steps.stepSummary: If a ישראל leaves his wine on a wagon or ship with a נכרי and goes by a shortcut, the wine stays permitted even if he went into town and bathed. If he announced he was going far away, the same time dispute applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone puts his wine on a wagon or a ship and goes off by a shortcut, even if he went into the city and bathed, the wine is permitted. If he told the נכרי he was going far away, it is forbidden if he was gone long enough to bore a hole, plug it, and let it dry. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: long enough to open the barrel, re-stop it, and let it dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: the owner leaves his wine traveling with a נכרי and goes another way himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the owner took a shortcut, the נכרי cannot know where or when he will meet up with him again. So even a long break, like going into the city to bathe, does not make the wine forbidden. Only an announced long absence brings back the time rule from step 8.

phrases.english: One who places his wine in a wagon or on a ship,
and went on his way by a shortcut,
even if he entered the city and bathed, it is permitted.
If he told him that he was going far away,
it is forbidden if there was enough time to bore a hole, plug it, and let it dry.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּפְתַּח אֶת הֶחָבִית, וְיִגּוֹף, וְתִיגּוֹב.
phrases.english: Enough time for him to open the barrel, stop it up, and let it dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה. It applies the same idea and repeats the same time dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine left on a wagon or ship while the owner travels by a shortcut stays permitted, even if he stopped in the city to bathe. An announced long absence brings back the time rule.

steps.title: Leaving a non-Jew alone in a shop
steps.stepSummary: If a ישראל leaves a נכרי in his shop and keeps going in and out, the wine is permitted. If he announced he was going far away, the same time dispute applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone leaves a נכרי in his shop, even though he keeps going out and coming in, the wine is permitted. If he told him he was going far away, it is forbidden if he was gone long enough to bore a hole, plug it, and let it dry. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: long enough to open the barrel, re-stop it, and let it dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third and last case: a נכרי left alone in a shop where wine is kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the owner keeps coming and going, the נכרי is always afraid he will walk back in, so the wine stays permitted. Again, only an announced long absence brings back the time rule. All three cases share one idea: what matters is whether the נכרי feels free to touch the wine without being caught.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out and comes in, meaning the owner is not there all the time

steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases, wine near a נכרי stays permitted as long as he thinks the ישראל could come back at any moment. Only after an announced long absence is the wine forbidden, and only if there was enough time to open and reseal a barrel without a trace. The תנא קמא measures that as boring and plugging a hole. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל measures it as replacing the whole stopper.

phrases.english: One who leaves a non-Jew in his shop,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֹּצֵא וְנִכְנָס — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: even though he goes out and comes in, it is permitted,
but if he told him that he was going far away,
it is forbidden if there was enough time to bore a hole, plug it, and let it dry.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּפְתַּח אֶת הֶחָבִית וְיִגּוֹף וְתִיגּוֹב.
phrases.english: Enough time for him to open the barrel, stop it up, and let it dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final case of the משנה. It uses the same rule and the same time dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי left in a shop while the owner keeps going in and out does not make the wine forbidden. An announced long absence brings back the time rule.

steps.title: Wine on the table versus wine on the side table
steps.stepSummary: A ישראל eating with a נכרי leaves the room. Wine on the main table is forbidden, and wine on the side table is permitted. If the ישראל told the נכרי to mix and drink, even the side-table wine is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a ישראל was eating with a נכרי at the table, with jugs of wine on the table and a jug on the side table, and he left the room, the wine on the table is forbidden and the wine on the side table is permitted. But if he told the נכרי, 'Mix yourself a drink,' even the side-table wine is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another case of a ישראל leaving his wine alone with a נכרי, this time at a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding question is which wine the נכרי would feel free to touch. Jugs on the table in front of him are within easy reach, so they are forbidden. A jug set aside on the side table is not something he would normally take, so it stays permitted. Once the ישראל invites him to pour and drink, the נכרי feels free to touch everything, so even the side-table jug becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A side table, set apart from the main dining table
Mix and drink (pour wine with water and help yourself)

steps.confusionAlert: The side-table wine is not permitted because the נכרי physically could not reach it. It is permitted because he would not feel free to take it. That is exactly why the invitation to 'mix and drink' changes the ruling.

phrases.english: If he was eating with him at the table,
and he left jugs on the table
and a jug on the side table,
and he left him and went out
what is on the table is forbidden,
what is on the side table is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: הֱוֵי מוֹזֵג וְשׁוֹתֶה
phrases.english: But if he said to him: Mix and drink,
even what is on the side table is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the משנה's list of situations where a ישראל leaves wine with a נכרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine on the table is forbidden and wine on the side table is permitted. An invitation to mix and drink forbids both.

steps.title: Open barrels versus sealed barrels
steps.stepSummary: Open barrels left with the נכרי are forbidden. Sealed barrels are permitted, unless the ישראל was gone long enough for the נכרי to open, reseal, and let the seal dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Open barrels are forbidden. Sealed barrels are permitted, unless he was gone long enough for the נכרי to open one, seal it again, and let the new seal dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a rule about barrels left in the room with the נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An open barrel is easy to touch, so it is forbidden. A sealed barrel shows no sign of tampering. The only worry is if there was enough time to open it and make a new seal that dried, leaving no trace. This is the longer measure that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gave in the earlier cases (steps 8–10), not the תנא קמא's measure of boring and plugging a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Reseal, and the new seal dries

steps.whatToRemember: Across the whole משנה, the test is whether the נכרי had the chance and the freedom to touch the wine without leaving a trace.

phrases.english: Open barrels are forbidden,
sealed ones are permitted,
[unless he was gone] long enough to open, reseal, and let it dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with the barrel rule, using the same time measure as before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Open barrels are forbidden. Sealed barrels are permitted unless there was time to open, reseal, and dry them.

steps.title: What does 'presumed to be watched' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking what situation the משנה meant by בְּחֶזְקַת הַמִּשְׁתַּמֵּר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the case of 'presumed to be watched'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for a definition of a phrase from the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 8, the משנה said wine carried by a נכרי is permitted if it is 'presumed to be watched.' The גמרא wants to know what situation actually counts as watched when the ישראל is not standing right there.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the case of
'presumed to be watched'?
phrases.notes: This phrase is quoted from the earlier part of the משנה about a נכרי carrying wine barrels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה into the גמרא and goes back to a phrase from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation counts as the wine being 'presumed to be watched'?

steps.title: The ברייתא about workers carrying pure items
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a ברייתא: if the workers carrying his pure items expect him around, the items stay pure even if he goes more than a מיל away. If he tells them he will come later, the items become impure once they are out of his sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone's donkey drivers and workers were carrying his pure items, even if he went more than a מיל away from them, his items stay pure. But if he told them, 'Go, and I will come after you,' once they are out of his sight, his items are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא about טהרות, which works the same way as the wine case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Watched' does not require the owner to be right there. If the workers think he might show up at any moment, they will be careful, so even a big distance does not matter. Once he announces that he will come later, they know they are on their own, so the moment he cannot see them, the items are treated as impure.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the model for the wine case. What matters is not physical distance but whether the people involved expect the owner might be watching.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
If his donkey drivers and workers
were carrying pure items,
even if he went more than a מיל away from them,
his pure items stay pure.
But if he said to them:
'Go, and I will come after you,'
once they are out of his sight,
his pure items are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by giving a parallel case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Watched' means the people carrying the items expect the owner might come back. Then even a big distance is fine. If he announces he is going away, the protection is gone once he loses sight of them.

steps.title: Why do the two halves of the ברייתא differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the first half of the ברייתא (pure) different from the second half (impure).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first part, and what is different about the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what makes the two halves of the ברייתא come out differently. This sets up רב יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both halves, the workers are out of the owner's sight. If being unwatched is a problem, it should be a problem in both. If it is not a problem, it should not be one in either. So the גמרא wants to know what real difference is behind the two rulings.

phrases.english: What is different about the first part,
and what is different about the last part?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What factor explains pure in the first half and impure in the second?
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's distinction between its first half (pure) and its second half (impure)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In both halves the same kind of workers are out of the owner's sight, so there seems to be no reason for the items to be pure in one half and impure in the other.

steps.title: רב יצחק: the workers were purified for this job
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק explains that in the first half, the owner had his workers purify themselves for this job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק said: The first part is a case where he purified his donkey drivers and workers for this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק answers the question by describing the first half as a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the workers themselves were made pure, their own touch does not make the items impure. That explains why the items stay pure in the first half even when the owner is far away.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes pure, here by having them immerse

phrases.english: רב יצחק said:
The first part is where he purified his donkey drivers and workers for this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the first half to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves seem to involve the same workers, so they should have the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the first half, the workers had been purified for the job.

steps.title: Then the second half should be pure too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the workers were purified, the same should be true in the second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the last part too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being purified protects the items, then the workers in the second half could also have been purified. So why would the items become impure there just because the owner said he would come later?

phrases.english: If so, the last part too?
phrases.notes: Meaning: if they were purified, the items should stay pure in the last case too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יצחק's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק's explanation of the first half
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Purifying the workers would seem to protect the items in the second half as well.

steps.title: An עם הארץ does not avoid others' touch
steps.stepSummary: The answer: even a purified עם הארץ is not careful about being touched by someone else, so he may have become impure along the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עם הארץ is not careful about contact with his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ruling of the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The workers' own purity is not enough. Once they are on their own, they might bump into another impure person and not care. Then they themselves become impure and pass it on to the items.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is not careful about purity laws

phrases.english: An עם הארץ is not careful
about contact with his friend.
phrases.notes: In other words, the worker may have touched someone impure on the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין עַם הָאָרֶץ מַקְפִּיד עַל מַגַּע חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a new source of impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Purifying the workers would protect the items in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Purified workers can still become impure by touching other people they meet.

steps.title: Then the first half should be impure too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: that same worry about touching others should apply in the first half as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us say that even in the first part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer around against the first half. In the next step רבא begins to answer this challenge, and his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an עם הארץ does not avoid other people's touch, the workers in the first half could also have touched someone on the way. Then the items should be impure there too. So the question of what difference the owner's announcement makes is back open.

phrases.english: If so,
let us say so even in the first part!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ רֵישָׁא נָמֵי נֵימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 18 against the first half.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the first half (pure), together with the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about touching others does not depend on whether the owner announced he was leaving, so it should make the first half impure too.

steps.title: רבא steps in to answer the challenge
steps.stepSummary: The words "אמר רבא" introduce a new voice who will answer the challenge from Step 19.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: the גמרא brings in רבא, who is about to answer the challenge raised in Step 19. His actual answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the גמרא pointed out that the worry about an עם הארץ touching other people should apply to both halves of the ברייתא. A new אמורא is now brought in, which signals a fresh approach to explaining the difference between the two halves.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבא's answer in these words. This line only tells us who is speaking, and his actual answer comes right after it.

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new speaker who will answer the challenge raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new explanation from a different אמורא; its content follows in the next part of the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge in Step 19 suggested there might be no real difference between the two halves of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא will offer a different way to explain the difference; the details come in the following text.
